results.corrected_title: Anthropic describes 'dreaming' as an offline process for organising and correcting agent memory
results.corrected_summary: Anthropic's engineering team published 'The components of agent memory' on 6 Nov 2026. The article describes 'dreaming', an offline process in which Claude reviews its past session logs and transcripts to organise memory and correct errors. Anthropic also says the process can build linked wiki pages and promote key notes to the context loaded at the start of each session. The article lists open questions, including compute cost and timing trade-offs.
key_facts: Published 2026-11-06 by Anthropic's Engineering team under the title 'The components of agent memory'.
Dreaming is an offline review of session logs and transcripts.
In a Pokémon example, a wrong note about a landmark's location trapped Claude. Dreaming tested the note against the transcripts and fixed it.
Open questions include compute cost and timing trade-offs.

results.corrected_title: Rep. Walkinshaw calls for permanent AI dialogue with China and safety testing of frontier models
results.corrected_summary: Rep. James Walkinshaw (D-Va.) told a GovExec event that the next Congress needs a 'permanent, serious' AI dialogue with China to reduce the risks of powerful models. He compared this to Cold War nuclear talks with the Soviet Union. He also said advanced AI models should be safety-tested, as the FAA inspects airplanes. These are statements of position, not policy.
key_facts: Walkinshaw called for 'permanent, serious' dialogue with China on AI risks, citing Cold War nuclear talks as precedent.
He compared safety testing of advanced AI models to FAA airplane inspections.
He is agnostic about whether a federal agency or a government-overseen third-party evaluator does the testing.
results.issues: Single source; remarks date possibly 5 Nov.
